title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded their Camaro, drew guns, and handcuffed them. Neighbor doorbell footage showed at least five patrol cars and a helicopter. Deputies had been looking for a stolen Camaro linked to multiple aggravated robberies. Flock cameras had picked up its plates, but an undercover deputy and helicopter could not read the plates on the car they stopped. After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car. Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot him, and he showed cuts and scrapes.

The men were not charged. Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants deputies held accountable and plans to hire an attorney. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said supervisors, including the district captain, shift lieutenants, and shift sergeants, will review body-worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
